newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BCE maize, wheat futures mixed, trade seen ebbing.
newsitem.headline: BCE maize, wheat futures mixed, trade seen ebbing.

text.p: Maize and wheat ended mixed on the Budapest Commodities Exchange (BCE) with traders expecting a gradual slowing of trade up to the end of the year.
Milling wheat contracts maturing in December dropped 370 forints to end at 27,810 forints, but this came as no surprise, dealers said.
"It is the last but one day of trade for December contracts and traders are liquidating," said Mihaly Otvos of OTP Forex.
Milling wheat contracts for July 1997 rose 170 forints to close at 22,000 while other maturities remained unchanged.
Maize futures prices were up 60 to 100 forints for March, May and July 1997 but eased 250 forints for November and 150 for December 1997.

"These changes do not amount to a trend," Otvos said referring to the latter figures which are based on expectations of next year's maize harvest. "There is too little information about 1997 to trade on".

Otvos saw activity winding down towards the end of the year as information is scarce, and said some market players were postponing activity until 1997 as they have made sufficient profit this year and do not want to widen their tax base.
Total turnover for the grain section was 459.8 million forints or 965 lots, of which 464 were maize and 490 milling wheat contracts.
Lot size is 20,000 kgs for all contracts.
The BCE announced earlier that grains futures trade, which currently runs for three days from Tuesday to Thursday, will be extended to all working days as of January 1.
